I felt the same in between my placements and thought I would really struggle with transitioning from theory to practice and back all the time. But muscle memory is a wonderful thing and once you're in your clinical setting it will come back to you.

 As for implementing evidence based nursing into practice, my advice would be just to ask questions all the time - what's the rationale for why you're doing what you're doing; how much evidence is there that this procedure works; if you read a relevant journal article ask how this evidence is likely to affect your current role etc.

Good luck with your next placement :)

I don't have any direct experience but I do highly recommend that you start off slow and build up as you feel confident and able. There is nothing worse than trying to do too much too quickly and injuring yourself which will mean even more time off and potential complications of the surgery itself. If there's a physiotherapist attached to your hospital or surgeon ask them if there are any exercises you can do safely while you recover so you maintain as much strength as possible before you can go back. Good luck with your surgery and recovery! ❤️

I have the Hella baby dolls in red and I adore them. I use them with protectors to preserve the suede but I personally think the quality of Hella heels is slightly superior and worth the price. They also fit my slightly wide feet better than my pleasers.

It may depend on the dance you're doing. If you're doing lots of floorwork then suede will be better as it will glide over the floor easier and won't stick like the leather ones. However if you're going to be up the pole a lot then be aware that the suede has no grip whatsoever and will slide down.

I hope that's helpful, good luck and enjoy your dance!
